body.statement: Can \(\widehat\Phi_n\) yield a multiplicity-calibrated test with asymptotically controlled familywise type-I error over rank-degenerate \(q\)-state models and acceptance probability tending uniformly to one when \(\min_{a,k,u}|d_{a,k,u}|\ge\kappa\) and \(\sigma_{q^K}(T_{12})\ge\kappa\) for fixed \(\kappa>0\)?
body.justification: Population zero-versus-nonzero decisions need calibrated separation before deployment.
body.gap: Gu et al. (2018) test provisional \(Q\)-matrix fit, while \(\texttt{cdmTools}\) checks binary structural criteria; neither handles adaptive categorical local-minor queries.
body.consumer: The routine can extend \(\texttt{cdmTools::is.Qid}\) with multiplicity-adjusted uncertainty and a failing-minor trace.

obligation.what_is_open: Derive a multiplicity-calibrated familywise type-I error bound and uniform separated power statement for the adaptive empirical query family after a sampling law has been added.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core specifies the formula for the empirical mass function but no probability law for the observations. For example, the observations could all repeat one arbitrary draw, in which case the empirical law need not converge to the observed law. Thus neither a type-I error probability nor bootstrap validity follows from the frozen primitives.
obligation.attempted: Reduced every raw rank query to a finite-dimensional perturbation bound and every reconstructed minor, away from singular intersections, to a continuous rational functional. This closes deterministic stability but cannot create stochastic convergence or calibration.
obligation.partial_result: For the finite population query family, every raw unfolding is a linear map of \(P_X\), so there is a finite constant \(C(q,K,J)\) such that \(\|\widehat U-U\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le C(q,K,J)\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\). The variational characterization \(\sigma_{\min}(U)=\min_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Uv\|_2\) and the triangle inequality then give \(|\sigma_{\min}(\widehat U)-\sigma_{\min}(U)|\le C(q,K,J)\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\). On a branch with simple spectrum and positive conditioning denominators, reconstructed local minors are continuous rational functions of \(P_X\). Consequently any deterministic sequence with \(\|\widehat P_n-P_X\|_{\infty}\to0\) eventually makes all decisions correctly whenever the stated \(\kappa\)-separation holds. A familywise probability guarantee, however, requires a sampling law and cannot be deduced from this deterministic statement.
